This oxygen atom is connected to an acyl/carboxylic acid fragment, in which a carbonyl C=O, a hydroxyl oxygen O–H connected to hydrogen, and the left R-substituted carbon chain can be seen. The figure also has curved arrows, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason and count: the problem requires counting all bonds participated in by non-hydrogen, including single bonds, double bonds, and triple bonds, but excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Therefore O–H is not counted. According to the visible non-hydrogen bond connections in the figure, the count is: P–Br 1, P–Br 1, P–O 1, C=O 1, C–O 1, C–C 1, C–R 1. The total is 1+1+1+1+1+1+1=7.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a phosphorus center bonded to two bromines and an oxygen, with that oxygen connected to an acyl/carboxyl fragment containing a carbonyl, an OH oxygen, and an R-substituted carbon chain.
